content:
maria: Heads-up: hit a crash when paged KV evicts during attention offload. Repro steps in replies.
kevin: timeline? which kernel path was active when eviction fired?
maria: Model: 7B, seq=2048, async attention offload path. Crash happens when a page fault fires inside `kv_fetch_async` while the attention kernel is iterating KV slots.
jena: Oof. Is the failure read-after-free or just stale pointer access?
maria: Stale pointer — kernel holds a raw pointer to a slot that got relocated by the pager compaction. No double-free, just invalid address access and SIGSEGV.
olga: Can you paste the minimal stack/logs? Also curious if this only surfaces under high fragmentation.
maria: Log excerpt:
```
attention_kernel.c:kv_step:245 assert(slot->valid) failed
kv_pager.c:compact:809 moved slot 0x7f9a3 -> 0x7f8b1
kernel_worker: thread 12 signal 11
```
kevin: Sounds like we assume slot stability during kernel execution. Two broad fixes: (A) kernel pins pages/slots for duration, or (B) pager exposes stable handles and only remaps behind an indirection table that kernels consult.
sunil: My take: implement a lightweight handshake where kernel asks pager for `kernel_handle = pager.acquire_handle(range, pin_hint)` which returns a stable id. Kernel uses `pager.resolve(handle)` to get current backing page. Pager can migrate backing pages but keeps handle stable. Eviction triggers `pager.on_evict(handle)` callback if migrate fails.
jena: That resolves staleness but adds indirection cost. Microbench shows resolve hit ~30ns if using a direct indirection array; pin/unpin costs dominate if we actually lock memory.
maria: Measured impact: pin/unpin per token ~= 0.5ms at batch=32 on A100 baseline. With handle indirection (no pin) overhead ~0.03ms/token. So handle-id approach looks promising.
olga: Edge case: what if pinned pages exceed RAM and pager must evict even pinned pages? Need eviction policy hooks so kernel can fall back to CPU attention path or a different model variant.
kevin: Proposal: add new kernel API surface:
```
struct handle { uint64 id; uint32 hint; };
handle acquire(range, pin_hint=false);
page_ptr resolve(handle);
void release(handle);
void on_evict(handle, reason);
```
Pager implements resolve as fast array lookup, acquire may optionally bump a pin refcount.
sunil: I'll draft an RFC: "kv-handle-indirection + eviction-callbacks". Will include benchmarks and migration plan. Plan to land non-pinning path first and measure.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary rollout for branch `kv-handle-indirection` at 2055554355 (r=olga)
olga: Running fragmentation stress + attention offload synthetic now, will post results in a bit :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jena: Also think about fallback policy: kernel should expose capability to switch to CPU attention path if >X% handles return evict reasons in the last T seconds.
maria: Agreed. For prod safety we should default to non-blocking resolve; if resolve fails (evicted) kernel retries with fallback. That keeps tail latency bounded.
kevin: Great. Action items: @sunil draft RFC and perf sheet, @olga run canary tests and collect traces, @jena work on fallback thresholds and telemetry counters, @maria prepare crash repro + deterministic test harness.
sunil: Will post RFC draft in #eng-ml by EOD tomorrow.
olga: Canary yields: no crashes so far at 1M steps, CPU fallback invoked ~0.7% under extreme fragmentation. Uploading traces to S3: s3://redwood-dev/kv-handle/canary/205555
maria: Nice. If canary stays clean, let's prioritize landing indirection path. Thanks y'all :rocket:
